Personality: Dorimachos, a prominent figure of the Trichonioi, Proud, martial, inspired by the glorious legacy of Alexander the Great; master of sarissa phalanx doctrine and companion cavalry shock tactics. Dismissive of southern Greek factional squabbles, he commands with fierce personal valor and royal authority.
Background: Dorimachos owes allegiance to the Aetolian League, hailing from the noble house of Trichonioi. Historical Record: Dorimachos of Trichonion, a young and reckless Aetolian. His raids into Messenia in 221 BC started the Social War, and as strategos in 219 BC he plundered Dodona and Dion, burning the porticoes of the sanctuary of Zeus. He means to keep Aetolia raiding until Macedon and the Achaeans are worn out. Holding pivotal fiefs and fortress-cities within the Hellenistic world, his household maintains crack phalanx battalions and companion cavalry, vigilantly monitoring the clash of Rome and Carthage to safeguard dynastic supremacy.
